title: Notarized macOS app, sandboxed local commands and deeper sources
summary: The macOS desktop app is now signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized, and the desktop app can run commands on your own computer inside a sandbox on macOS, Windows and Linux. Research reports, citations, sources and the MCP catalog all gain substantial features. Update packages remain Tauri-signed on the Preview channel; Windows installers are not publisher-signed, and stable/latest promotion is unchanged.
items: The macOS app and its disk image are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized, so macOS opens them without a Gatekeeper warning. Updating from v0.3.0-rc.8 changes the app's signing identity: macOS may ask once for keychain access and for the microphone and screen-recording permissions again.

The desktop app can run commands on your computer in a sandbox on macOS, Windows and Linux (on Linux through the .deb package). The sandbox runtime is downloaded on request and its signature is verified. Private and local network addresses are always blocked, and each device can require approval for other hosts or restrict commands to an allowlist, with outbound connections recorded.
The desktop app shows a startup screen while the web app loads, and offers a retry when the server cannot be reached.
Research runs produce editable, versioned report deliverables whose sources link back to the evidence, and tables keep their headings on every PDF page.
Citations point to the passage that supports them, including when the answer and the source are in different languages.
Sources gain a Source Guide, answers can be saved as notes, web sources can be discovered from a topic and imported, and a Google Drive connector syncs the files you pick.

Public MCP pages list a server's tools with their revision history, an overview and a quality scorecard, group entries for the same product, and let publishers claim and correct their own entries. Servers can be installed through an install.md for agents and the CLI, and members choose between OAuth and an API key when connecting.
HTML artifacts can keep page data between visits. Owners can export or clear it, shared data and external links need confirmation, and public data collections are chosen per artifact.

Chat runs are more robust: reasoning and tool output are stored once, a failed model attempt is withdrawn before a retry streams, Stop survives a page reload, and a run's working and closing phases are bounded by wall-clock limits.

Speech and documents: speech-to-text handles long audio by splitting at pauses, text-to-speech converts to the requested format, and DeepSeek is available as a provider for web search, OCR, speech-to-text and text-to-speech.
Pro and Team seats are $9.90 per month with 8,000 credits, prices show cents, and speech is billed by audio seconds and characters. A public pricing page is available.

Public catalogs are easier to find and keep clean in search: sitemaps cover the full MCP and Skill catalogs, duplicate catalog pages stay out of the index, category pages show totals, and authors can add a Listed on SourceWeft badge to their README.

Operations and security: web and API responses carry security headers, production logs report privacy-safe activity, and dependency updates clear the current audit advisories, including Next.js 16.4.2.
